title: Tilted Seasons
tagline: Why does summer flip across the equator?

science.hiddenLaw: Earth's axial tilt ε≈23.5° makes solar declination δ vary annually as δ≈ε·sin(orbital longitude), so daily-mean top-of-atmosphere insolation at latitude φ varies as I ∝ (1/r²)[H₀·sinφ·sinδ + cosφ·cosδ·sinH₀] via solar zenith angle and day-length H₀; r-variation from eccentricity is <7% and globally in-phase, so seasons are opposite in opposite hemispheres and vanish if ε=0.
science.plainStatement: We have seasons because Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5 degrees. The tilt tips the Northern Hemisphere toward the Sun in June and away in December (opposite for the Southern Hemisphere), making sunlight hit more directly and days longer in summer and the opposite in winter. Earth's distance from the Sun changes very little and is not the cause.
misconceptions: Seasons are caused by Earth being closer to the Sun in summer and farther in winter due to an elliptical orbit — predicts both hemispheres have summer at perihelion (January) and winter at aphelion.
The tilt works by changing Earth's distance to the Sun, or the Sun gets stronger/weaker with seasons — predicts no opposite seasons and no latitude dependence of day length.

If distance caused seasons, all latitudes would warm and cool together and the equator would have large seasons — predicts no systematic opposite phase between 45°N and 45°S and no polar amplification of seasonality.

rules.source: exports.init = (params, rng) => { return { day: 0, currentInsolation: 0, temp: 15, history: [], maxIns: -Infinity, minIns: Infinity, sumIns: 0, juneIns: null, decIns: null, janIns: null, julyIns: null }; }; exports.step = (state, params, rng) => { const tiltRad = params.tiltDeg * Math.PI / 180; const ecc = params.eccentricity; const latRad = params.latitudeDeg * Math.PI / 180; const day = state.day; const M = 2 * Math.PI * day / 365; const rFactor = Math.pow(1 + ecc * Math.cos(M), 2); const lambda = 2 * Math.PI * (day - 80) / 365; const sinDelta = Math.sin(tiltRad) * Math.sin(lambda); const delta = Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, sinDelta))); let H0; const cosH0 = -Math.tan(latRad) * Math.tan(delta); if (cosH0 <= -1) H0 = Math.PI; else if (cosH0 >= 1) H0 = 0; else H0 = Math.acos(cosH0); let term = 0; if (H0 !== 0) { term = H0 * Math.sin(latRad) * Math.sin(delta) + Math.cos(latRad) * Math.cos(delta) * Math.sin(H0); if (term < 0) term = 0; } const insolation = rFactor * term / Math.PI; let temp = state.temp; temp = temp + (insolation * 80 - temp) * 0.08; const history = state.history.slice(); history.push(insolation); if (history.length > 365) history.shift(); let maxIns = state.maxIns; let minIns = state.minIns; if (insolation > maxIns) maxIns = insolation; if (insolation < minIns) minIns = insolation; const sumIns = state.sumIns + insolation; let juneIns = state.juneIns; let decIns = state.decIns; let janIns = state.janIns; let julyIns = state.julyIns; if (day === 172) juneIns = insolation; if (day === 355) decIns = insolation; if (day === 15) janIns = insolation; if (day === 196) julyIns = insolation; return { day: day + 1, currentInsolation: insolation, temp: temp, history: history, maxIns: maxIns, minIns: minIns, sumIns: sumIns, juneIns: juneIns, decIns: decIns, janIns: janIns, julyIns: julyIns }; }; exports.observe = (state, params) => { const hist = state.history; const n = hist.length || 1; const max = state.maxIns === -Infinity ? 0 : state.maxIns; const min = state.minIns === Infinity ? 0 : state.minIns; const mean = state.sumIns / n; const range = mean > 1e-9 ? (max - min) / mean : 0; const ratio = min > 1e-9 ? max / min : 0; const juneMinusDec = (state.juneIns !== null && state.decIns !== null) ? state.juneIns - state.decIns : 0; const julyMinusJan = (state.julyIns !== null && state.janIns !== null) ? state.julyIns - state.janIns : 0; return { daily_insolation: state.currentInsolation, ground_temp: state.temp, annual_insolation_range: range, summer_winter_insolation_ratio_45N: ratio, june_minus_dec_insolation: juneMinusDec, july_minus_jan_insolation: julyMinusJan }; }; exports.view = (state, params) => { const day = state.day; const angle = 2 * Math.PI * day / 365; const ecc = params.eccentricity; const r = 35 * (1 - ecc * ecc) / (1 + ecc * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * day / 365)); const cx = 50 + r * Math.cos(angle); const cy = 50 + r * Math.sin(angle); const ins = state.currentInsolation; const tNorm = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (ins - 0.05) / 0.35)); const rCol = Math.round(40 + tNorm * 200); const gCol = Math.round(120 + tNorm * 80); const bCol = Math.round(255 - tNorm * 180); function toHex(v){ let s=v.toString(16); return s.length===1 ? '0'+s : s; } const earthColor = '#' + toHex(rCol) + toHex(gCol) + toHex(bCol); const sunColor = '#ffcc00'; return { kind: 'bodies', bounds: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 100, h: 100 }, bodies: [ { id: 'sun', x: 50, y: 50, radius: 8, color: sunColor }, { id: 'earth', x: cx, y: cy, radius: 4, color: earthColor } ] }; };

checks.description: Control: with zero tilt and circular orbit, annual insolation range at 45° latitude vanishes — removing tilt removes seasons
With Earth-like tilt 23.5° and circular orbit, summer insolation at 45°N is >2× winter insolation
Tilt predicts opposite seasons: at 45°N June insolation exceeds December insolation
Tilt predicts opposite seasons: at 45°S June insolation is less than December insolation (June is winter in south)
Refutes distance misconception: at 45°N July insolation exceeds January insolation even though Earth is nearer the Sun in January (perihelion), so tilt dominates over distance
